description: The figure presents a set of stacked bar charts illustrating the “Meaningful Variability Share” (MVS) and its complement (1–MVS) for two model sizes (“70B llama” and “8B llama”) across four domains titled “Health and Nutrition,” “Logistics,” “Personal Finance,” and “Travel and Transportation.” In each domain panel, the horizontal axis contains the two categorical model labels in the same left-to-right order (“70B llama” then “8B llama,” with the text angled), and the vertical axis shows proportions on a linear scale from 0 to 1.0, with regularly spaced tick marks at approximately 0.2 intervals. Each bar is stacked to a total height of 1.0 and uses a legend where MVS is shown in teal/green and 1–MVS is shown in blue. In “Health and Nutrition,” the “70B llama” bar has an MVS segment of about 0.59 with the remaining ~0.41 as 1–MVS, while the “8B llama” bar shows MVS near 0.39 and 1–MVS near 0.61. In “Logistics,” “70B llama” shows MVS around 0.51 and 1–MVS around 0.49, and “8B llama” shows MVS around 0.48 with 1–MVS around 0.52. In “Personal Finance,” the “70B llama” bar has MVS near 0.72 and 1–MVS near 0.28, while “8B llama” has MVS near 0.36 and 1–MVS near 0.64. In “Travel and Transportation,” “70B llama” shows MVS around 0.39 and 1–MVS around 0.61, and “8B llama” shows MVS around 0.37 with 1–MVS around 0.63. The bars are not displayed as being sorted by value, and there are no additional visual emphases such as outlines or annotations beyond the color-coding and panel titles.
